tasks.title: Carry side in the draft marker
tasks.acceptance:
- `cr draft` renders every block's marker with `side` between `path` and `start_line`, per §7.1.1, and triage reads it back: a LEFT record's marker says `side=LEFT`, and an unchanged draft posts as rendered.
- An edited `side` is re-validated per §6.1.2 like `path`, `start_line` and `line` in §7.2's table: a LEFT-to-RIGHT edit that no longer resolves aborts with exit code 1 naming the record id, and one that resolves re-anchors. A marker missing `side` is refused with exit code 1 naming the record id and the grammar.

tasks.closed_reason:

tasks.title: Compute waiver and index keys before sending
tasks.acceptance:
- `cr post --confirm` reads every tree the §7.4.1 waiver keys of the draft's discards and the §9.3.6 posted-index keys of the payload's records need before `post_unresolved` is set and before the request. A read that fails refuses the post with exit code 3 and a hint, with no network write, no `post_unresolved`, and posted.json, findings and waivers left as they were. After a successful request cr writes the keys it already computed and reads no checkout or pull request.
- Proven through the command in internal/cli tests: with a key tree that cannot be read, the gh shim logs no POST and the round is still postable once the tree is readable. With readable trees, a post whose checkout read would fail after the request still marks the records posted, writes the waivers and the index entries, and clears `post_unresolved`. `cr post --reconcile` keeps working when it adopts a review.
- go test -race -count=1 of the edited packages passes.
tasks.closed_reason:
- cr post --confirm now forms every waiver key of the draft's discards (discardWaivers) and every posted-index entry of the payload's unposted records (postedEntries) in sending.formKeys (internal/cli/send.go), called right after the post_unresolved refusal and before posted.json, the sent sections, post_unresolved and post.Create.
- A read that fails returns the read's own error wrapped in "round N was not posted and nothing was sent", so it exits 3 with that cause's hint (git.CommandError, gh errors, state.FileError), with no gh POST and nothing written; TestAKeyTreeThatCannotBeReadRefusesThePostBeforeAnythingIsSent compares the whole state root byte for byte before and after.
- After a successful request, storeKeys writes the precomputed waivers through writeWaivers and markPosted walks the precomputed records and appends the precomputed entries through writeAdopted/appendPostedIndex, stamped with the created review id, with no tree read; TestAKeyTreeThatStopsReadingAfterTheRequestLeavesThePostWhole counts zero key reads after the POST.
- internal/cli/postkeys_test.go drives cr post --confirm with a gh shim on PATH: with the discard's or the posted record's key tree failing, the shim logs no POST, exit is 3 with the git hint, and the state root is unchanged.
- In both rows the same round then posts once the tree reads: one POST, a pull-request waiver for the discard, and one index entry for f1.
- With a tree that fails once the shim has logged the POST, the records are posted and discarded, the waiver and the index entry (review PRR_shim) are written, and post_unresolved is cleared; cr post --reconcile still forms its index at adoption through the same postedEntries and the existing reconcile tests (TestAnUnresolvedPostingIsReconciledToAnAdoptAndToAClear, reconcileownround, reconciletriage, draftunresolved) pass; all three new cases fail with the previous send.go, posted.go, reconcile.go and regenerate.go mapped in through go test -overlay.

tasks.title: Close the SIGKILL window at runner start
tasks.acceptance:
- A SIGKILL of `cr` between starting the test runner and recording its process group can no longer leave an unrecorded runner: the runner is held on a pipe until the group is recorded, so a killed `cr` closes the pipe and the runner never starts, without changing how `tests.cmd` argv is executed; if that cannot be done without a shell wrapper, record the run's intent before start and have the next command report a possible orphan instead, and say which was chosen and why in the closure.
- Proven with an injected kill between start and release: no runner process exists afterwards and the sandbox holds no mutation; the ordinary path still records the run.
- The release notes' SIGKILL limitation is removed or corrected, and go test -race -count=1 of the edited packages passes.
tasks.closed_reason:
- A test runner started with a runner lock is now held on a pipe until its process group is recorded: sandbox.RunExit starts cr's own binary under argv[0] cr-held-runner with the resolved program and the runner's argv, an init in internal/sandbox/run.go waits on fd 4 (state.AwaitRunnerRelease) and only on a released byte calls syscall.Exec of that program with the same argv and environment, while a cr killed before RunnerLock.Started and RunnerHold.Release closes the pipe so the held process reads EOF and exits 125 having run nothing; exec failures come back over a close-on-exec fd 5 as the same fork/exec PathError Start gave (internal/state/runnerhold.go).
- Option 1 was chosen over the recorded-intent fallback because it closes the window instead of reporting it and needs no shell: it is an init rather than a cobra command, so the command tree is unchanged, and the only pinned test it touches is TestOnlyTheStatePackageWritesToTheFilesystem, whose processControl list in internal/cli/norepowrite_test.go now names Exec beside Kill, since exec writes no path.
- A measurement through a go test overlay running the same python probe as tests.cmd under HEAD's run.go and under this one printed byte-identical argv (including an empty and a spaced argument), cwd, environment hash, descriptor table (0 chr, 1 and 2 fifo, 3 the runner lock), blocked signals, ignored signals, RLIMIT_NOFILE, group leadership and umask, and identical errors for a missing program and a PATH lookup failure.
- TestACrKilledBeforeItsRunnerIsReleasedLeavesNoRunner in internal/cli/runnerhold_test.go spawns cr probe run --kind mutation with sandbox.BeforeRunnerRelease set only in the test binary to SIGKILL cr between the start and the release of the mutation run, then asserts cr died on SIGKILL with the mutation on disk, no process holds the runner lock, the runner's mutation-only pid file never appeared, every run the runner script observed read the head source, no group was recorded and no probe stored.
- The same test then runs cr test and asserts its honesty is exactly the one recreation notice for app.go with no stopped-runner notice, the sandbox holds the head's app.go and so no mutation, and the ordinary path appended one run record with exit_code 0, tests_run 4 and tests_failed 0.

tasks.title: Copy .env.testing into the laravel-pest sandbox
tasks.acceptance:
- The shipped laravel-pest profile's `sandbox.copy` is `[".env", ".env.testing", "vendor"]`, so a clone holding a gitignored `.env.testing` gets it in the sandbox and Laravel resolves the test database the way the developer's own run does.
- Proven through `cr sandbox create` on a fixture clone: with `.env` and `.env.testing` both land in the sandbox; with only `.env` the absent entry is skipped with the existing notice and creation succeeds.
- go test -race -count=1 of the edited packages passes.

tasks.title: Update unedited shipped profiles on cr init
tasks.acceptance:
- `cr init` rewrites a profile file under `~/.cr/profiles/` whose bytes equal a previously shipped version of that profile (v0.1.0, v0.2.0 or v0.2.1) with the current shipped bytes, leaves a file equal to the current version alone, and leaves any other file alone with a notice naming it; its output reports which files it updated.
- The previous versions' bytes come from testdata extracted from each tag's builtin JSON (as `cr init` wrote them), not a hand-typed hash list, and a test fails when a tag carrying a builtin profile is not covered.
- Proven through `cr init` in both directions: a byte-equal v0.2.1 file is rewritten and reported; the same file with one key edited is not touched and is named; go test -race -count=1 of the edited packages passes.

tasks.title: Name a stale shipped profile when it loads
tasks.acceptance:
- Every command that loads a profile whose bytes equal a previously shipped version of it says so under `honesty`, naming the version and that `cr init` updates it (e.g. that the shipped profile changed `sandbox.copy`); a profile equal to the current shipped bytes, or edited, gets no line; no command writes a profile at load time.
- Proven through `cr test` (or `cr brief`) with a byte-equal v0.2.1 file (line present) and an edited one (no line), sharing s2's version data; go test -race -count=1 of the edited packages passes.

tasks.title: Print an experiment header naming env files
tasks.acceptance:
- Before the runner starts, `cr test` and `cr probe run` print a header (standard error, so a JSON document on standard output stays whole) naming the runner argv, the sandbox path, the clone root's gitignored `.env*` files and which of them the sandbox holds, and every such file absent from the sandbox and not in `sandbox.copy`, with `sandbox.copy` named as the fix; for a probe whose §5.2.2 unfiltered baseline runs first, the header says the whole suite runs first as the baseline. `cr sandbox create` reports the same uncopied files under `honesty`. The clone's ignored files are listed through internal/git's runner; no file content is read.
- Proven through the commands: a clone with gitignored `.env` and `.env.testing` both copied → header lists both, no missing line; a gitignored `.env.local` not in `sandbox.copy` → the line names it; the header appears on `cr test`, on a filtered probe, and on the implicit baseline with the baseline sentence; JSON output on standard output is unchanged.
- go test -race -count=1 of the edited packages passes.
